title: Homebrew joints and house-party dancing in Prohibition
summary: What a homebrew joint was, musicians playing house parties, and dances of the era.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: The homebrew, John? Well, I sold homebrew them. It was doing prohibition. They didn't have anybody's house, anything. There's any little hole in the wall there. They just set up, put the top, ice it up with icing. You had your homebrew there for twenty-five or fifteen cents a bar, whatever it was. You used to have these house parties and all that. Always had your homebrew and all that. You used to have some good times.
And the musicians would come in and play at these things? Oh yeah. Did they dance to music lights in there?
And the party that people would... What kind of dancing did they do? Did they do the Charleston then or that was after the dance?
